scenes.title: Orchestrating dbt + Spark + Ingestion End-to-End
scenes.narration: This capstone lesson ties everything together, showing how an orchestrator coordinates ingestion, Spark, and dbt into one reliable end-to-end pipeline.

scenes.title: The end-to-end pipeline
steps: Ingest raw data to the lake
dbt transforms and tests in the warehouse
scenes.narration: A production data platform usually chains several tools. First an ingestion step lands raw data in the lake or warehouse, then Spark handles heavy processing of large or messy files that SQL alone cannot manage, then dbt takes over to model and test the data inside the warehouse, and finally the polished marts are published and stakeholders alerted. The orchestrator's role is to make these very different tools behave as one coherent pipeline.

scenes.title: The orchestrator's responsibilities
bullets: Wait for data readiness before each stage
Retry transient failures and alert on real ones
Give one place to observe the whole run
scenes.narration: Across such a heterogeneous pipeline the orchestrator carries four responsibilities. It enforces correct ordering so dbt never runs before Spark finishes, it waits for data readiness before each stage begins, it retries transient failures while alerting on genuine ones, and it provides a single pane of glass to observe the entire run from ingestion through publication.

scenes.title: Wiring the stages in Airflow
scenes.code:
with DAG('platform_daily', schedule='@daily', catchup=False) as dag:
    ingest = PythonOperator(task_id='ingest', python_callable=load_to_lake)

    spark = SparkSubmitOperator(task_id='spark_clean', application='clean.py')

    with TaskGroup('dbt') as dbt:
        run = BashOperator(task_id='run', bash_command='dbt build')

    ingest >> spark >> dbt
scenes.narration: This DAG expresses the full flow. A Python task ingests data into the lake, a SparkSubmitOperator runs the heavy cleaning job, and a TaskGroup wraps the dbt build so the transformation stage reads as a single unit. The dependency chain at the end guarantees ingestion completes before Spark, and Spark before dbt. Using dbt build rather than dbt run means every model is tested immediately, so bad data halts the pipeline before it ever reaches the marts.

scenes.title: Two integration styles for dbt

left.heading: Single dbt build task
points: dbt manages its own internal DAG

right.heading: Model-level tasks
points: Each dbt model becomes an Airflow task
Fine-grained retries and lineage in the UI

scenes.narration: There are two ways to run dbt inside the orchestrator. The simplest is a single build task, where one operator runs dbt build and dbt handles its own internal DAG, which is easy but gives only coarse visibility. The richer approach explodes each dbt model into its own Airflow task, often generated automatically by a tool like Cosmos, so you get per-model retries and see dbt's lineage right inside the orchestrator's UI at the cost of more complexity.

scenes.title: What makes it production-grade
bullets: Every stage is idempotent and safe to rerun
Data-aware triggers instead of guessed timers
Deferrable sensors keep workers free while waiting
Clear alerting and SLAs on the critical path
scenes.narration: Several disciplines separate a fragile pipeline from a production-grade one. Every stage should be idempotent so any run can be safely retried, data-aware triggers should replace timers that merely guess when data is ready, deferrable sensors should hold long waits without tying up workers, and clear alerting with service-level agreements should guard the critical path so problems surface fast.

scenes.text: A great platform lets each tool do what it does best while the orchestrator guarantees ordering, readiness, retries, and end-to-end observability.
scenes.narration: The capstone takeaway is that a great data platform lets each tool do what it does best, with ingestion, Spark, and dbt each in their lane, while the orchestrator ties them together by guaranteeing correct ordering, data readiness, resilient retries, and end-to-end observability across the whole run.
